label: Predynastic and Protodynastic
summary: Regional iconographies and cults develop while Upper and Lower Egypt move toward a unified state.

label: Early Dynastic, Dynasties 1–2
summary: Kingship and state cult consolidate; early monumental and mortuary patterns take shape.

label: Old Kingdom, Dynasties 3–6/8
summary: Pyramid building and solar kingship. The earliest surviving Pyramid Texts appear in late Dynasty 5, initially for kings.

label: First Intermediate Period
summary: Political fragmentation and stronger local power centers; older royal mortuary resources spread and change.

label: Middle Kingdom, Dynasties 11–13/14
summary: Reunification, the rise of Amun at Thebes, Coffin Texts on nonroyal coffins, and major Sobek patronage in the Fayum.

label: Second Intermediate Period
summary: Hyksos rule in parts of Lower Egypt. Later memory connects foreignness and Set in complicated ways.

label: New Kingdom, Dynasties 18–20
summary: Imperial wealth, huge Theban temples, royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings, the Underworld Books, the Book of the Dead, and dense documentation of personal piety.

label: Amarna episode
summary: Akhenaten elevates the Aten, attacks Amun's name, relocates the court, and centralizes divine access through the royal family.

label: Third Intermediate Period, Dynasties 21–25
summary: Political decentralization, elaborate coffins and mummification, animal cults, and shifting foreign and Nubian rule.

label: Saite and Late Period, Dynasties 26–31
summary: Archaism and renaissance. Native and Persian rule alternate, some traditions intensify, and Set is increasingly vilified in many contexts.

label: Ptolemaic Period
summary: Greek-speaking rulers support Egyptian temples. The surviving temple programs at Edfu, Dendera, Kom Ombo, Esna, and Philae formulate learned local theologies.

label: Roman Period
summary: Temple traditions and Demotic and Greek magical practice continue while Egyptian deities circulate across the Mediterranean. Older institutions eventually contract.

label: Pyramid Texts
summary: Carved first in late Dynasty 5 royal pyramids, later used by queens and, in altered form, by others. The corpus never fully disappears.

label: Coffin Texts
summary: Written on nonroyal coffins mainly in the First Intermediate Period and Middle Kingdom, overlapping with older and later material.

label: Underworld Books
summary: The Amduat, Book of Gates, and related compositions map the night hours in New Kingdom royal tombs.

label: Book of the Dead
summary: Individualized spell collections on papyrus and other media, used from the New Kingdom into the Greco-Roman period.

label: State temple institutions
summary: Royal and delegated temple service maintaining cult images, offerings, and the created order.

label: Royal mortuary evidence
summary: Pyramids, royal tombs, and their inscribed programs dominate the surviving record for long stretches.

label: Personal-piety evidence
summary: Votives, stelae, letters, oracle questions, and settlement material make household and individual practice unusually visible, above all at Deir el-Medina.
